articles.title: Democrats win the Arizona House, Senate and governor’s office for the first time since 1966
articles.summary: PHOENIX (AP) — Democrats in Arizona won control of both legislative chambers and retained the governor's office, giving the party its first trifecta in the s...
articles.body:
PHOENIX (AP) — Democrats in Arizona won control of both legislative chambers and retained the governor's office, giving the party its first trifecta in the state since 1966 as Democrats made major gains nationwide in this week's elections and took control of both chambers of Congress .

In her first term, Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs had vetoed more than 540 measures passed by the Republican-led Legislature on policies including taxes, immigration and voting laws. Hobbs has said she's looking to address water issues and affordability, and take on fraud and abuse in the state's school voucher program.

The Associated Press called enough legislative races to confirm that both chambers flipped on Friday. The news organization calls races individually and it can take several days after voting, depending on when election officials tally the votes and how close the elections are. There have not been major disputes or disruptions this year.

In Arizona, Republicans have held the House for 60 years and the Senate since the early 1990s.

Overall, Democrats took full control — both statehouse chambers and governors' offices — in at least six states where they previously shared power with Republicans. Besides Arizona, those wins were in the battleground states of Michigan, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Nevada and Wisconsin.

The flips weren't just in states that are normally competitive. Democrats won control of the Texas House, which Republicans have held since 2003, and elected Gina Hinojosa as the state's first Democratic governor since George W. Bush ousted Ann Richards in 1994. Republicans held onto the state Senate.

Democrats also flipped the lower chambers of the legislature in North Carolina and both chambers in New Hampshire, where Republican Kelly Ayotte was reelected. The count could grow as results are tallied in additional states.

The National Council of State Legislatures says it's likely to end up as the election with the most legislative seats and chambers changing parties since the 2010 election, when Republicans took over governments across the country amid the Great Recession.

Democrats will also hold the governor's office in at least 28 states. Results are still pending in Alaska and Kansas.

This story first moved on Nov. 6, 2026. It was updated on Nov. 9, 2026, to correct that although Democrats gained a majority in the Maine House in the midterm election, they had previously held a plurality in the state's lower chamber and controlled it with the help of independent lawmakers.

articles.title: Ministros do STF dizem que encerrar inquérito das fake news servirá para 'virar página' no país | G1
articles.standfirst: Arquivamento de inquérito aberto em 2019 foi defendido pela PGR nesta segunda-feira. Para Gonet, apurações feitas ao longo dos sete anos devem ser mantidas em sigilo.
articles.summary: Arquivamento de inquérito aberto em 2019 foi defendido pela PGR nesta segunda-feira. Para Gonet, apurações feitas ao longo dos sete anos devem ser mantidas em sigilo.
articles.body:
Ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) afirmaram, reservadamente, à TV Globo nesta segunda-feira (9) que o encerramento do inquérito das fake news vai representar um "passo importante" e "uma página virada" na história do tribunal .

A medida é vista como "simbólica" e a "conclusão de um ciclo". Segundo esses ministros, o inquérito cumpriu uma função importante de preservar a atuação e a legitimidade de integrantes da Corte. Mas, no atual cenário, o desfecho da investigação não teria apoio unânime no tribunal.

A Procuradoria-Geral da República defendeu, nesta segunda-feira (9), o arquivamento do chamado inquérito-mãe das fake news , com a continuidade dos procedimentos abertos de forma individualizada.

Agora, cabe ao presidente do STF, Edson Fachin , analisar o parecer da PGR e decidir sobre o fim do inquérito. O magistrado já afirmou anteriormente que o inquérito deverá seguir para o "arquivamento definitivo".

Fachin assumiu a relatoria do inquérito em setembro, em meio à crise institucional instalada no Supremo diante dos desdobramentos das investigações do caso Master.

As apurações atingiram integrantes da Corte diante de menções e indicações de proximidade de ministros com o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, preso na operação Compliance Zero.

De lá para cá, a presidência do STF passou a fazer um pente-fino em mais de 100 procedimentos vinculados ao inquérito das fake news. Ao menos nove foram arquivados e outros tiveram pedidos de providências enviados à Polícia Federal e à PGR.

O fim do inquérito das fake news começou a ser discutido internamente ainda na presidência do ministro aposentado Luís Roberto Barroso. Em conversas reservadas, Barroso vinha debatendo com o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, que era o relator, a conclusão do inquérito.

Com a saída de Barroso, Fachin assumiu as tratativas internas pelo fim do inquérito, já no fim do ano passado. O presidente do Supremo vinha analisando com Moraes um prazo razoável.

A crise do Banco Master, no entanto, acabou pressionando Moraes e levando Fachin a assumir a condução do desfecho do inquérito. No STF, a expectativa é de que Fachin arquive o inquérito-mãe e que a decisão seja tomada em breve.

A investigação foi aberta em março de 2019 por iniciativa do então presidente do Supremo, Dias Toffoli, que designou Alexandre de Moraes como relator.

O foco inicial era apurar ataques e ameaças aos ministros e ao STF, mas ao longo dos anos o inquérito teve seu objeto ampliado e alcançou até mesmo um integrante da Corte: André Mendonça.

A apuração reúne operações policiais, bloqueios de redes sociais, prisões e denúncias oferecidas pela Procuradoria-Geral da República. E virou alvo de críticas de entidades, como a Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil.

No pedido de arquivamento feito ao Supremo, a PGR defendeu o inquérito .

"Ameaças dirigidas aos ministros e a seus familiares, campanhas de desinformação financiadas e difundidas em massa e incitações ao fechamento do Tribunal voltavam-se contra a liberdade de decidir e a autoridade das decisões; projetavam, enfim, as suas repercussões sobre a preservação da ordem constitucional", afirmou a PGR.

O procurador-geral, Paulo Gonet, também apontou que a extensão do inquérito foi uma necessidade diante dos riscos.

"A extensão temporal deste inquérito encontrou correspondência na sucessão de ameaças que, ao longo de sete anos, foram identificadas às condições de livre e independente exercício da função jurisdicional pelos integrantes do Supremo Tribunal Federal", declarou.

A PGR também se manifestou pela manutenção do sigilo dos dados reunidos ao longo dos sete anos do inquérito das fake news. A investigação soma mais de 12 mil folhas.

A Procuradoria argumentou que a investigação alcançou um amplo universo de pessoas, mas possui dados sensíveis que devem ser preservados.

"O acervo reunido nestes autos ao longo de 7 anos guarda informações de elevada sensibilidade estratégica, relativas à segurança estrutural e institucional dos Ministros do Tribunal e de altas autoridades da República", afirmou Gonet.

"Os autos registram ameaças e elementos atinentes à integridade física e operacional de agentes públicos no exercício de funções centrais do Estado; a sua divulgação tem o potencial de expor ao espaço público cogitadas vulnerabilidades que a investigação buscou proteger", completou.

De acordo com a PGR, em mais de 50 volumes, o inquérito reúne dados pessoais, bancários, fiscais e empresariais de empresas, instituições e investigados.

Na avaliação da Procuradoria, o levantamento integral do sigilo do inquérito tem potencial para causar uma exposição negativa, uma vez que a Constituição admite a restrição da publicidade para defender a intimidade ou o interesse social.

"O interesse público em conhecer fatos relevantes para a vida comunitária se encontra, aqui, atendido pela publicidade das ações penais e das decisões respectivas. Não há presumir, entretanto, que semelhante interesse prepondere sobre a proteção devida aos dados e à privacidade de quem atravessou a investigação sem a cristalização de indícios suspeitos. Aqui, é forçosa a apreciação casuística dos dados a serem abertos", disse.

Gonet afirmou ainda que as pessoas e empresas mencionadas podem pedir diretamente acesso aos elementos.

Fachada do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), em Brasília, com estátua da Justiça em destaque. — Foto: Divulgação/STF

articles.title: Presidente de time preso por tráfico e bets ilegais vai para casa | G1
articles.standfirst: Sebastião Lauze Queiroz de Amorim foi preso durante a Operação Ludus Sordidus, em 2025. Ele tem uma doença cardíaca grave, deverá usar tornozeleira eletrônica e só poderá sair de casa para atendimento médico.
articles.summary: Sebastião Lauze Queiroz de Amorim foi preso durante a Operação Ludus Sordidus, em 2025. Ele tem uma doença cardíaca grave e deverá usar tornozeleira eletrônica.
articles.body:
Sebastião Lauze Queiroz de Amorim foi preso em Cuiabá — Foto: Reprodução

A Justiça de Mato Grosso determinou, na última sexta-feira (6), que o presidente de um time de futebol amador, Sebastião Lauze Queiroz de Amorim , volte à prisão domiciliar em Cuiabá . Ele tem uma doença cardíaca grave e, segundo a decisão, órgãos do estado deixaram passar mais de cinco meses sem realizar a perícia que deveria avaliar se ele recebia tratamento adequado na Penitenciária Central do Estado (PCE).

Sebastião havia voltado à penitenciária em setembro de 2025 , após a Justiça revogar uma primeira prisão domiciliar por descumprimento de medidas cautelares. Agora, o juiz Jean Garcia de Freitas Bezerra, da 7ª Vara Criminal de Cuiabá, voltou a autorizar o cumprimento da prisão em casa por razões humanitárias, ao considerar que a demora no atendimento colocou a saúde do réu em risco.

O g1 tentou localizar a defesa de Sebastião, mas não havia conseguido até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A avaliação cardiológica chegou a ser agendada para junho de 2026 no Hospital Estadual Santa Casa. Quando Sebastião foi levado ao hospital, em agosto, a equipe constatou que a unidade fazia atendimentos especializados, mas não realizava perícias. A Secretaria de Estado de Saúde indicou a Perícia Oficial e Identificação Técnica (Politec), que atribuiu a responsabilidade à Secretaria de Estado de Justiça (Sejus).

O juiz deu cinco dias para que a Sejus providenciasse a perícia ou um atendimento especializado equivalente. A secretaria confirmou o recebimento do pedido em 29 de setembro. Segundo a decisão, mais de um mês depois, a pasta ainda não havia informado uma data nem apresentado justificativa.

A família também pagou por consultas com cardiologista e angiologista e por um eletrocardiograma, após a própria penitenciária indicar a opção de atendimento particular. A defesa enviou os comprovantes em junho, mas, segundo o juiz, os atendimentos aparentemente não chegaram a ser agendados.

O Ministério Público de Mato Grosso (MPMT) apoiou a mudança para prisão domiciliar diante da demora na perícia e de relatos de piora na saúde de Sebastião. O órgão sugeriu um prazo inicial de 60 dias. O juiz determinou a apresentação de relatórios médicos mensais e estabeleceu que a medida poderá ser reavaliada a qualquer momento.

A decisão determina que a tornozeleira eletrônica seja instalada na saída da penitenciária. Sebastião deverá informar à Justiça o endereço onde cumprirá a prisão domiciliar e só poderá sair para atendimentos médicos previamente agendados e comunicados ao juízo ou em caso de urgência médica.

Em ambos os casos, ele terá 24 horas após o atendimento para comprovar que foi atendido. Também está proibido de manter contato com os demais réus do processo por qualquer meio. O descumprimento de uma das condições levará ao retorno à penitenciária , conforme a decisão.

Por que ele havia voltado à penitenciária

Sebastião foi preso em agosto de 2025 na Operação Ludus Sordidus , que investigou a atuação de uma facção em esquemas de tráfico de drogas, jogos de azar, estelionato e lavagem de dinheiro. Segundo a Polícia Civil, ele chefiava o grupo na região dos bairros Jardim Liberdade e Osmar Cabral, em Cuiabá, e recebia 10% dos lucros de uma plataforma clandestina de apostas.

Na época, a Justiça autorizou a prisão domiciliar após um laudo apontar a doença cardíaca e o risco de infarto . Ele voltou à penitenciária em 8 de setembro de 2025. Segundo a Polícia Civil, durante o período em casa, ele teria continuado a praticar crimes e se reunido com integrantes da facção.

Na nova decisão, o juiz reavaliou a suspeita de que Sebastião teria usado a primeira prisão domiciliar para incitar represálias pela morte do irmão, morto em confronto com a polícia. Segundo o magistrado, as denúncias anônimas citadas na investigação não mencionavam Sebastião diretamente, e os documentos analisados não traziam provas concretas de que ele tivesse participado das ações atribuídas a outros réus.

O juiz considerou que ainda havia risco de novos crimes ao impor as restrições da prisão domiciliar.

articles.title: PGR encaminha a Fachin parecer pelo arquivamento do inquérito das fake news | G1
articles.standfirst: Pedido de arquivamento vale para inquérito principal, chamado de 'inquérito-mãe'. Documento é assinado pelo procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet, que afirma que o objeto da investigação se esgotou.
articles.summary: Pedido de arquivamento vale para inquérito principal, chamado de 'inquérito-mãe'. Documento é assinado pelo procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet, que afirma que o objeto da investigação se esgotou.
articles.body:
A Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) encaminhou nesta segunda-feira (9) ao presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), Edson Fachin , parecer favorável ao arquivamento do inquérito das fake news.

O pedido de arquivamento vale para o inquérito principal, chamado de "inquérito-mãe", de número 4.781.

Outros 103 procedimentos foram abertos em decorrência da investigação principal, entre petições e investigações preliminares em diferentes fases processuais ( entenda mais abaixo ).

O documento é assinado pelo procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet , que afirma que o objeto da investigação se esgotou.

Os procedimentos derivados do inquérito que ainda estão em andamento deverão seguir para análise caso a caso.

Edson Fachin já tinha determinado o arquivamento de oito investigações ligadas ao inquérito das fake news . Os demais procedimentos deverão ser analisados individualmente. O que já foi julgado não será alterado.

Essa é uma das últimas etapas para que Fachin encerre o inquérito . Ele assumiu o comando do processo depois de retirar a relatoria do ministro Alexandre de Moraes , em setembro.

Na época, em meio à crise no STF envolvendo os ministros Alexandre de Moraes e André Mendonça e às discussões sobre as investigações do caso Master, o presidente do STF decidiu retirar de Moraes a relatoria do inquérito das fake news.

Fachin também passou a arquivar parte desses procedimentos e encaminhou os casos para manifestação da PGR. Agora, Gonet se manifestou pelo arquivamento definitivo do inquérito principal.

Conselho Superior do Ministério Público Federal rejeita abrir investigação sobre a atuação de Paulo Gonet no caso Master — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Aberto há sete anos para investigar ataques, ameaças e notícias falsas contra o STF e seus ministros, o chamado inquérito das fake news acumulou, ao longo dos anos, decisões que ampliaram o alcance da investigação e geraram controvérsias dentro e fora da Corte.

Ao longo dos anos, deu origem a diferentes investigações e medidas, como bloqueios de contas em redes sociais, buscas e apreensões e quebras de sigilo.

Em setembro, Fachin assumiu a relatoria e afirmou que a mudança buscava estabelecer "segurança jurídica" e uma "adequada delimitação institucional". Desde antes de assumir o processo, o atual presidente do STF já defendia o encerramento do inquérito.

articles.title: Fux suspende afastamento da juíza Gabriela Hardt, punida pelo CNJ por atos na Lava Jato | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro considerou que punição estava prescrita; magistrada poderá voltar ao trabalho após licença médica e terá vencimentos integrais.
articles.summary: Ministro considerou que punição estava prescrita; magistrada poderá voltar ao trabalho após licença médica e terá vencimentos integrais.
articles.body:
O ministro Luiz Fux , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), suspendeu o afastamento da juíza Gabriela Hardt, determinado pelo Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) por atos praticados durante a Operação Lava Jato.

➡️Ao conceder a liminar, Fux afirmou que houve prescrição da punição.

Segundo o ministro, o CNJ já tinha conhecimento dos fatos envolvendo Hardt em março de 2019, mas o processo administrativo disciplinar só foi instaurado em junho de 2024, depois do prazo de cinco anos previsto pelas regras do conselho.

Luiz Fux também considerou que não havia provas de que Gabriela Hardt tivesse agido intencionalmente para cometer uma irregularidade, buscado beneficiar a si própria ou terceiros ou participado das negociações do acordo investigado.

Para o ministro, Hardt não pode ser responsabilizada disciplinarmente apenas por ter tomado uma decisão judicial posteriormente anulada ou considerada equivocada. Segundo Fux, é preciso demonstrar que houve efetiva infração funcional ( entenda mais abaixo ).

Com a liminar, ficam suspensos o afastamento das funções, a redução dos vencimentos e a contagem do prazo da punição até o julgamento definitivo do mandado de segurança.

Na prática, Gabriela Hardt volta a ter direito aos vencimentos integrais do cargo. Quando foi afastada pelo CNJ, a juíza continuou recebendo salário, mas deixou de ter direito a gratificações e outros benefícios vinculados ao exercício da função.

A decisão ainda permite que Hardt volte à função após o fim da licença médica, desde que não exista outro impedimento legal.

A decisão também garante à magistrada os vencimentos integrais do cargo. Hardt já continuava recebendo salário durante o afastamento, mas, com a punição, perderia gratificações e outros benefícios vinculados ao exercício da função.

Segundo dados do CNJ obtidos pela reportagem, o último contracheque disponível é de setembro, quando Hardt recebeu R$ 51,5 mil, sem descontos.

Luiz Fux em sessão plenária do STF — Foto: Alejandro Zambrana/STF

Na decisão, Luiz Fux afirmou que o prazo para o CNJ punir Gabriela Hardt já havia terminado quando o processo administrativo disciplinar foi instaurado.

Pelas regras do CNJ citadas pelo ministro, o prazo de prescrição para uma falta funcional de magistrado é de cinco anos, contado a partir do momento em que a administração toma conhecimento do fato.

Segundo Fux, o CNJ tomou conhecimento da conduta atribuída a Hardt em 15 de março de 2019, quando foi protocolada uma reclamação disciplinar sobre a homologação do acordo.

Já a decisão do conselho que determinou a abertura do processo administrativo disciplinar foi concluída somente em 7 de junho de 2024.

O ministro calculou que transcorreram cinco anos, dois meses e 23 dias entre os dois momentos. Para Fux, portanto, a punição estava prescrita.

Ele rejeitou o entendimento adotado pelo CNJ de que somente uma investigação iniciada em 2023 teria dado ao órgão conhecimento suficiente das circunstâncias da conduta.

Fux afirmou ainda que Hardt não poderia ser responsabilizada disciplinarmente apenas por ter tomado uma decisão judicial que posteriormente foi anulada ou considerada equivocada. Para o ministro, seria necessário demonstrar que a magistrada cometeu uma infração funcional.

Na avaliação de Fux, a questão é saber se uma magistrada pode ser punida por uma decisão que, segundo ele, foi tomada de boa-fé, de forma fundamentada e sobre uma questão inédita, mas que posteriormente recebeu entendimento diferente do Supremo.

“Juízes que decidem sob a ameaça de punição pelo resultado de suas decisões não são juízes independentes, e um Judiciário sem independência não serve ao combate à corrupção, à Operação Lava Jato ou a qualquer outra causa pública: serve a quem, a cada momento, tiver o poder de punir”, afirmou Fux.

Fux apresentou ainda outros fundamentos para suspender a punição. Entre eles, afirmou que:

não ficou comprovado que Hardt participou das negociações do acordo ou buscou benefício próprio ou de terceiros;

algumas das cautelas cobradas posteriormente da magistrada não tinham, segundo Fux, base normativa em 2019;

e a aplicação da pena máxima de dois anos de disponibilidade não teria sido suficientemente individualizada.

A análise é liminar, ou seja, provisória. O mérito do mandado de segurança ainda será julgado. Fux determinou que o CNJ preste informações em dez dias e que, depois, o processo seja encaminhado à Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR).

Por que Gabriela Hardt foi punida pelo CNJ

O CNJ decidiu, em agosto deste ano, afastar Gabriela Hardt do cargo por dois anos por atos praticados durante sua atuação na Operação Lava Jato.

A punição foi aprovada por unanimidade. Por 10 votos a 4, o conselho fixou em dois anos o período de afastamento.

A apuração foi aberta em 2024, depois que uma fiscalização da Corregedoria apontou supostas irregularidades na validação, por Hardt, de um acordo que previa a criação de uma fundação privada abastecida com recursos relacionados à Lava Jato. Os valores chegariam a R$ 2 bilhões.

Hardt havia homologado o acordo em 2019, quando atuava na 13ª Vara Federal de Curitiba, responsável pelos processos da Lava Jato.

Ela assumiu a vara provisoriamente depois que o então juiz Sergio Moro deixou a magistratura para integrar o governo de Jair Bolsonaro. Atualmente, Hardt atua na 23ª Vara Federal em Curitiba.

Esse não foi o primeiro afastamento de Hardt relacionado à apuração sobre atos da Lava Jato.

Em abril de 2024, o então corregedor nacional de Justiça, ministro Luis Felipe Salomão, determinou o afastamento de Hardt e de outros magistrados. No dia seguinte, porém, o plenário do CNJ derrubou o afastamento de Hardt por 9 votos a 6.

Na ocasião, Luis Roberto Barroso, então presidente do CNJ e do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), afirmou que o afastamento de um magistrado dependeria de decisão da maioria absoluta do conselho e não poderia ser determinado individualmente pelo corregedor.

articles.title: Lula embarca para a COP31 na Turquia em 1ª viagem após reeleição | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Antália, presidente fará o primeiro discurso internacional após a reeleição. Lula transmitirá a presidência da Conferência do Clima à Turquia e à Austrália.
articles.summary: Lula viaja à Turquia para a COP31, onde apresenta resultados ambientais do Brasil e transmite a presidência do clima em seu primeiro giro após a reeleição.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) embarcou nesta segunda-feira (9) para Antália, na Turquia, onde participará da 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (COP31).

A previsão é que Lula chegue ao país ainda na noite desta segunda. A terça (10) está reservada para a preparação para o evento, mas podem acontecer reuniões bilaterais ainda não definidas.

Apesar da COP31 começar nesta segunda, a cúpula de líderes será nos dias 11 e 12 de novembro , quando Lula participa.

Esta será a primeira agenda internacional de Lula após a reeleição ao Palácio do Planalto, no dia 25 de outubro .

O presidente Lula, o assessor Celso Amorim e o deputado André Janones (Rede-MG) durante viagem à Turquia — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

A comitiva do governo brasileiro, que embarcou de Brasília nesta manhã, é composta por:

João Paulo Capobianco, ministro do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima

Fernanda Machiaveli, ministra do Desenvolvimento Agrário e Agricultura Familiar do Brasil

Alexandre Silveira, ministro de Minas e Energia

André de Paula, ministro da Agricultura e Pecuária

Márcio Elias Rosa, ministro do Desenvolvimento, Indústria e Comércio Exterior

Guilherme Boulos, ministro da Secretaria-Geral da Presidência

embaixador André Correa do Lago, ⁠presidente da COP30

Laudemir Müller, ⁠presidente da ApexBrasil

Aloizio Mercadante , presidente do BNDES

Celso Amorim , assessor especial para assuntos internacionais

Mauricio Lyrio, secretário de Clima, Energia e Meio Ambiente do Ministério das Relações Exteriores

Lula convidou o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), e o presidente da Câmara dos Deputados, Hugo Motta ( Republicanos -PB), para integrarem a comitiva em viagens internacionais.

Além da COP31, o chefe do Executivo vai para a cúpula da Associação de Nações do Sudeste Asiático (Asean) nas Filipinas.

Hugo Motta agradeceu o convite, mas decidiu ficar em Brasília para tocar a pauta de votação da Casa. O presidente da Câmara firmou também que tem poucas semanas até o recesso de final de ano – e com pautas de interesse do próprio governo.

O presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre, também não embarcou para a Turquia com Lula. A previsão é de que o parlamentar conduza as sessões da Casa desta semana. Existe também a possibilidade de Alcolumbre convocar uma sessão do Congresso Nacional para os próximos dias.

Janones publicou uma foto com Lula no avião; deputado faz parte da comitiva do petista para a COP31 — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Na Cúpula de Líderes, Lula transmitirá a presidência da COP à Turquia e à Austrália, depois de o Brasil ter sediado a conferência de 2025, em Belém (PA). O governo brasileiro vai reforçar a importância da continuidade dos compromissos assumidos na edição anterior.

Na sexta-feira, Lula participou de reunião do Conselho Nacional de Política Energética (CNPE) e destacou que chegaria à COP31 com uma proposta para que o mundo diminuísse a dependência de combustível fóssil.

“O mais importante é que o Brasil não fala teoricamente: o Brasil apresenta propostas. Propostas de um país que descobriu o pré-sal, um país que descobriu muito petróleo na margem equatorial brasileira, e mesmo assim a gente continua sendo país que vai levar avante a diminuição até chegar o dia de não precisar mais de combustível fóssil”, disse na ocasião.

O presidente também destacou que vai apresentar que a queda das taxas de desmatamento no Brasil e os avanços na implementação Fundo Florestas Tropicais para Sempre (TFFF).

Interlocutores do governo afirmam que o presidente recebeu pedidos de outros países para encontros, mas, até o momento, nenhuma conversa bilateral foi agendada.

João Paulo Capobianco, ministro do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima, afirmou que a presidência brasileira entregará os documentos dos mapas do caminho para afastamento do uso de combustíveis fósseis e fim do desmatamento até 2030, propiciando o seguimento desse debate iniciado na COP28, em Dubai, quando foi aprovado o Primeiro Balanço Global (GST1) do Acordo de Paris.

A expectativa é que Lula também mostre os resultados conquistados pelo Brasil, fazendo inclusive o contraponto com a gestão anterior, do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro.

Segundo o ministro do MMA, alguns dos pontos apresentados serão:

Avanços na operação do Fundo Amazônia, “que ficou paralisado nos quatro anos do governo anterior, mas recuperou capacidade de captação de recursos com a ampliação do número de países doadores e já destinou, nos três anos meio do governo Lula, R$ 7,6 bilhões para projetos e programas de proteção e uso sustentável da Amazônia”.

Redução de 560 milhões de toneladas de gases de efeito estufa entre os anos de 2022 e 2024;

Redução do desmatamento em todos os biomas brasileiros;

Apresentação do Mapa do Caminho Brasileiro para a Eliminação do Desmatamento e da Degradação Florestal até 2030.

Na sexta-feira (13), Lula embarca para as Filipinas, onde busca a renovação do certificado de importação da carne brasileira. Será a primeira visita de um chefe de Estado brasileiro ao país asiático.

O presidente brasileiro participa, pela segunda vez, da 49ª Cúpula da ASEAN – primeiro foi convidado pela Malásia e, agora, pelas Filipinas.

O governo brasileiro participa com o intuito de firmar novos parceiros comerciais, especialmente em um contexto pós-tarifaço norte-americano.

Outro chefe de governo que participa do evento é Donald Trump . Este pode ser o primeiro encontro entre os presidentes brasileiro e americano após a reeleição de Lula e a vitória dos democratas nas midterms dos EUA.

articles.title: Lula viaja e deixa para volta definição de nomes de futura equipe e medidas para garantir equilíbrio fiscal | G1
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) viaja e deixa para a volta a definição dos primeiros nomes de sua futura equipe . Mais importante, deixa para depois do giro internacional a decisão sobre as medidas fiscais para garantir o equilíbrio das contas públicas.

O mercado esperava algum sinal mais concreto do presidente Lula em seu pronunciamento de domingo (8) sobre as medidas fiscais que irá adotar, mas o governo já havia avisado que ele não anteciparia nada em sua fala à nação.

A novidade é que, se na eleição chegou a dizer que não se preocupava com o tamanho da dívida pública, agora afirma que, sim, está preocupado com sua trajetória.

O fato é que, tal como em 2022, quando ganhou do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, agora, em 2026, Lula viaja para participar da 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças Climáticas (COP31) , na Turquia, deixando para sua volta a definição de temas vitais para o seu quarto mandato:

os primeiros nomes de sua futura equipe;

mais importante, as medidas fiscais para garantir o equilíbrio das contas públicas;

o nome que indicará ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) e enviará ao Senado ainda neste ano.

O presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), defende o nome de Rodrigo Pacheco , enquanto petistas defendem o advogado-geral da União, Jorge Messias, que foi rejeitado em abril deste ano.

Depois da Turquia, Lula segue para as Filipinas, em uma viagem de Estado, e retorna ao Brasil no início da próxima semana.

Em 2022, durante sua primeira viagem internacional depois de vencer a eleição, ele definiu os nomes de Fernando Haddad para a Fazenda, Marina Silva para o Meio Ambiente e Mauro Vieira para as Relações Exteriores.

Agora, dificilmente anunciará durante a viagem quem será seu futuro ministro da Fazenda.

Segundo assessores, Lula só vai definir o chefe da equipe econômica depois de analisar as medidas que estão sendo elaboradas pelo atual ministro da Fazenda , Dario Durigan, e que serão apresentadas ao presidente após seu retorno do giro internacional.

Dario Durigan e o ministro do Planejamento, Bruno Moretti, vão preparar um ajuste fiscal que garanta o cumprimento da meta fiscal do próximo ano, sem exceções, preservando os programas sociais do governo Lula.

articles.title: Kirk finds Dave Chappelle’s joke about husband’s murder ‘beyond disgusting’
articles.summary: Erika Kirk, the widow of the late conservative activist Charlie Kirk, condemned comedians and political commentators for joking about political violence afte...
articles.body:
Erika Kirk, the widow of the late conservative activist Charlie Kirk, condemned comedians and political commentators for joking about political violence after Dave Chappelle said during a stand-up performance that he had been in a "good mood" since her husband's assassination.

"To see leftist podcasters, comedians, and commentators laugh about political assassination as though it's entertainment and the destruction of a human life is a punchline, is beyond disgusting," Erika Kirk wrote in a post on the social platform X .

She did not name Chappelle in her post but criticized those who have made light of her husband's killing.

"My husband, Charlie Kirk, was killed in an act of political violence, something our two children and I will live with every day for the rest of our lives," she continued.

Charlie Kirk, the founder of Turning Point USA and a prominent ally of President Trump, was fatally shot while speaking at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025. He was 31.

"A culture that laughs at assassination is one of profound moral decay. It threatens the very foundation of our country and the principles that hold our democracy together," Erika Kirk wrote on X. "You do not have to agree with someone's politics to recognize the value of their life. This should not be so hard. Political violence must never be something this country tolerates, excuses, or celebrates."

Chappelle made the remark Saturday during a sold-out show at Madison Square Garden in New York City, according to footage circulating on social media.

"I feel f---ed up saying this. It's scary being a public speaker," Chappelle told the audience. "Ever since that guy Charlie Kirk got murdered — and I shouldn't say this publicly — but, I feel better."

Chappelle previously discussed Kirk's killing in his Netflix comedy special "The Unstoppable," released three months after the shooting. At the time, he said the assassination had shaken him as someone who also speaks publicly for a living.

"If you talk for a living and see Charlie Kirk get murdered that way, I'm going to be honest," he said. "I was shook."

articles.title: Joe Biden to scale back book tour as cancer ‘slows me down’
articles.summary: Former President Joe Biden said his tour to promote his presidential memoir “Promise me, America,” will be scaled back, as he continues to battle cancer.
articles.body: Former President Joe Biden signaled he will have to scale back the tour to promote his upcoming memoir “Promise me, America,” as he continues to undergo treatment for cancer. “Some days are better than others,” Biden wrote in a lengthy post on X on Sunday. “It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down.” As a result, Biden said he would no longer “be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped. However, I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves.” Months after leaving office in January 2025, Biden, 83, announced that he had been diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer and has since undertaken courses of radiation therapy and hormone treatment. Last year, his office also shared that he had undergone surgery to remove cancerous skin cells. The memoir is due out on Nov. 17 and details his four years in the White House, including “the decisions I made, and why I made them,” he wrote. “More than anything, it’s about my faith in the American people and the great American experiment in self-governance and democracy.” In August, his son, Hunter Biden, told the BBC in an interview that his father’s cancer had spread to other parts of his body and was causing him pain, even as he continues to speak out on public issues. “The cancer has spread, metastasized into his bones and further,” Hunter Biden told the BBC in August. “It’s very painful and it’s very debilitating in many respects.” “It’s really sad to watch,” he added. Former first lady Jill Biden also previously told NBC News: “I think Joe will live with cancer till the rest of his life.” Biden was the oldest man to serve as U.S. president and his age and health were a source of concern for much of his time in office. The memoir of the 46th president delves into “his campaign, his presidency, his decision to run again,” according to the publisher, Hachette Book Group. It also “reveals the deeply agonizing calculation behind his decision in the summer of 2024 to step aside from the presidential race and to put his party and the nation before his personal ambitions.” Biden suspended that re-election bid and ultimately endorsed his vice president, Kamala Harris, after mounting pressure to step aside. Biden has frequently defended himself against accusations about his mental acuity and memory. Biden said in the post Sunday that his doctors were “encouraged by how I’ve responded to treatment,” and thanked the public for their prayers and well wishes as he vowed to keep fighting.

articles.title: Centrist Democrats warn party leaders not to ‘go too far’ after midterm wins
articles.summary: Democrats just won what could be their largest House majority in decades. But some battle-tested centrists are already warning their party not to lose it in...
articles.body:
Democrats just won what could be their largest House majority in decades but some battle-tested centrists are already warning their party not to lose it in 2028.

Those now-emboldened Democrats, who have long competed in battleground districts, are now urging party leaders to stick to this fall's core promises on affordability — or risk a backlash in the next election.

Privately and publicly, these Democrats are urging leaders to focus on kitchen-table issues and avoid culture-war fights they believe could divide the party and invite Republican attacks, according to nearly a dozen lawmakers and aides.

For many, that means steering clear of transgender issues and policing reform bills they fear Republicans would weaponize. They also want to avoid left-wing priorities such as ending US support for Israel or abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Several Democrats also called for restraint in the party's oversight agenda, warning that talk of impeaching President Donald Trump or his Cabinet should not overshadow that focus.

"We've got to be very careful that we don't go and do everything," Rep. Henry Cuellar, a battleground Democrat who's survived previous red waves, told CNN. "I just hope that we don't get carried away, get caught up in these fringe issues."

"It's like a rubber band, it'll snap back," he recalled telling then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi's team roughly two decades ago as he argued that issues like cap-and-trade climate change legislation could contribute to a 2010 wipeout.

Centrists like Cuellar had been in retreat since the end of the Biden era, watching their party move left in primary after primary. Many expected next year's Democratic caucus to be the most liberal in history, with an insurgent wing of democratic socialists wielding power .

Now, Democrats in purple and red seats insist they will be the most powerful bloc in next year's House. The party will have to defend more than 50 Democrats in seats Trump won — compared with a far smaller number this cycle.

That sets up a potential clash with an equally emboldened far left — which just saw its strongest-ever election cycle, ousting a slate of Democratic incumbents this year.

Several of the most progressive House members, including Reps. Ro Khanna and Delia Ramirez , are already calling to "abolish ICE" and "block the bombs" next year. Rep. Ayanna Pressley has added to that list : "Don't just talk about racial justice—pass reparations NOW."

"We are going to try to govern, progressives are going to try to make a point," one Democratic aide working for a centrist member told CNN. "This is not the time to show how progressive we can be. People need to see us fighting."

Balancing those factions will fall to House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is on a path to become the next speaker.

Centrists believe Jeffries understands his mission: deliver on affordability and protect his new incumbents in battleground seats in two years. At the same time, members such as Khanna are pressing him to hold key floor votes on priorities such as Medicare for All.

Many also believe liberal Democrats in Jeffries' orbit, including Congressional Progressive Caucus Chair Greg Casar of Texas, share that focus. In a post-election memo to his members, Casar wrote: "Our top priority will be passing populist policies that deliver on Democrats' promise to end the affordability crisis," according to a copy obtained by CNN.

Rep. Greg Stanton of Arizona, a senior member of the centrist New Democrat Coalition, said voters gave Democrats control of Congress to do one thing: lower the costs of food, housing, health care and energy.

"If we get too far afield from those things, we could lose trust with the American people," said Stanton, whose name is sometimes floated as a contender to be the next House campaign chief.

"Democrats dominated this election and yet we still need to govern with the humbleness of knowing that the election was a reaction to people being pissed off at Trump and House Republicans. We still need to earn the trust of the American people if we want a durable majority."

Centrist Democrats are also urging caution in the push to hold Trump and his administration accountable. Many of these members fear there could be a rank-and-file push to impeach a new Cabinet secretary every few weeks. Some are unsure they would go beyond impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, according to multiple people familiar with internal discussions.

"They need to be very thoughtful and deliberate on what sort of impeachment investigations strategy is pursued," said Phil Gardner, a senior adviser for the moderate campaign group Blue Dog Action, which helped double the number of moderate Blue Dog Democrats in the House next year.

"There is so much corruption, so many things to be outraged about, that it could very quickly end up consuming the entirety of the caucus if we're not careful," Gardner said, adding: "Impeachment is a very grave decision."

One of Jeffries' biggest challenges next year will be defining the party's health care agenda, as even some Democrats in red seats advocate Medicare for All.

Democrats agree on Jeffries' early goals: vote to restore billions of dollars in Obamacare subsidies and prevent steep Medicaid cuts next year.

Beyond those goals, pressure is mounting for party leaders to embrace the left's push for universal health care, despite widespread unease in the caucus. Populist Democrats such as Sam Forstag in Montana and Bob Brooks in Pennsylvania ran on issues such as Medicare for All — and won.

"I think everybody in this country should have the choice to join Medicare," Forstag said in an interview with CNN days after he won. He added that seniors in his district have only a single provider to choose from for Medicare Part B plans, while people with private insurance have only two choices — both of which just dramatically raised rates.

"I am, and we should all be, very angry that the last time Democrats had unified control of our government, they made tiny piecemeal incremental changes, and they applied Band-Aid solutions instead of actually fixing our healthcare system," Forstag told CNN, summing up his push for big change.

Jeffries has distanced himself from the left's signature Medicare for All bill, aggravating his more liberal members.

But that has reassured many moderates who want to avoid a major intraparty fight over healthcare reform, particularly with Trump in the White House. They recall how poorly the debate ended for them in 2010.

"He doesn't need to swing for the fences on day one in the way that some might demand," one moderate Democrat told CNN. "If we go too far, we lose the House in 2028."

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: Trump's FAA touts new AI-powered tool helping thousands of passengers avoid flight delays
articles.summary: The Trump administration's SMART system rerouted nearly 180 flights carrying 24,000 passengers, cutting flight times by over 10 minutes on average.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE: The Trump administration's new AI-supported air traffic management tool has already helped reroute nearly 180 flights carrying approximately 24,000 passengers to avoid congestion, cutting flight times by more than 10 minutes on average, according to new Department of Transportation (DOT) data shared exclusively with Fox News Digital. The Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories system, known as SMART, has been operational for nearly six weeks, helping air traffic controllers identify more fuel-efficient routes and anticipate potential disruptions. According to DOT, the technology has also saved nearly 80 gallons of fuel per flight on average, offering an early glimpse of how the Trump administration hopes to reduce flight delays and cancellations. TRUMP UNVEILS AMERICA.GOV AS AI-POWERED HUB FOR PASSPORTS, MEDICARE ENROLLMENT AND MORE "Under President Trump, we are making historic progress to revitalize air traffic control and improve the passenger experience for millions of Americans," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital. Duffy also said the technology would deliver broader benefits as the program expands. "SMART will slash frustrating delays, reduce stress on air traffic controllers, and lower travel prices." One example came in October when a flight carrying 147 passengers from Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport to Orlando International Airport avoided expected congestion after SMART recommended an alternative route. SEVERE TURBULENCE DIVERTS NEW YORK CITY FLIGHT TO MIAMI, 8 INJURED The flight had been scheduled to depart during a period when congestion was expected along its original path. SMART identified a route farther west, which air traffic controllers accepted, shortening the journey by 11 nautical miles and saving six minutes of flight time, according to DOT. The technology combines 200 data streams, including weather patterns, flight paths, traffic flow and controller staffing metrics, into a centralized platform. Its AI-supported engine helps aviation specialists anticipate where congestion could develop and recommend more efficient routes before congestion builds. The technology is also designed to improve how the FAA manages severe weather, a source of disruptions for U.S. air travelers. PILOTLESS CARGO AIRCRAFT COULD CHANGE HOW PACKAGES MOVE According to a DOT fact sheet, the agency's existing approach involves blocking off large rectangular sections of airspace affected by storms, even though weather systems are often irregularly shaped, and safe corridors may remain available. SMART is intended to provide a clearer picture of changing weather conditions, allowing aviation specialists to identify routes around storms and determine when restricted airspace can safely reopen. Despite its AI-supported capabilities, SMART does not independently direct aircraft or replace human air traffic controllers. A team of aviation specialists analyzes and validates SMART's data before sending scheduling recommendations to the FAA's Air Traffic Control System Command Center. Those recommendations are then forwarded to local air traffic control facilities, where officials decide whether to accept them. The initiative comes as the nation's busiest airports handle millions of flights annually. According to DOT, approximately 6.5 million flights operate each year at the nation's 30 busiest airports. About 300,000 receive reroutes before departure, while 3.6 million experience airborne reroutes, vectoring or holding. The FAA initially limited SMART's rollout to the National Capital Region in September before beginning validation efforts with air route traffic control centers in Miami, Jacksonville and Atlanta in October. The agency plans to continue testing the system as it works toward expanding SMART to all 22 air traffic control centers nationwide. For travelers, the Trump administration's goal is fewer delays for passengers, shorter flights and less time lost to flight congestion.

articles.title: JOHN MIZE: Democrat victory just means the fight for life has added importance
articles.summary: Tuesday, Nov. 3 election losses leave mifepristone's pending review among several vital pro-life battlegrounds, as we face a pro-abortion Congress.
articles.body: Tuesday, Nov. 3, Americans cast their votes and turned congressional majorities against the pro-life cause. It may be easy to despair, especially following two years of strong, pro-life leadership that accomplished a historic year of defunding many abortion providers from federal Medicaid dollars, but the pro-life movement has fought through hostile waters before — and won. Here’s how we navigate the next two years. STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE Defending legacy pro-life provisions must be a first priority. We have known for months that the Hyde Amendment, protecting taxpayers from being forced to directly fund abortions, has been in the crosshairs for the next pro-abortion Congress. But conscience protections for healthcare entities that choose not to provide abortions under the Weldon Amendment may also be on the line. This pro-abortion majority wants to make Americans complicit in their extremism. Both the Hyde and Weldon amendments have survived pro-abortion majorities before, including the 117th Congress. In 2021, the House Appropriations Committee advanced a Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education spending bill that omitted both Hyde and Weldon rider language. Even though both chambers were led by pro-abortion majorities, pro-life organizations were able to rally, telling Congress that these protections are not up for negotiation. This is the same message we must carry over the next two years. Congress must also be reminded that preserving these riders is in its own best interest, attaining bipartisan public support. According to the 2026 Knights of Columbus/Marist polling, 54% of Americans opposed taxpayer funding of abortion and 63% support conscience protections for healthcare providers. 'EXTREMIST' AND 'BARBARIC': MASSACHUSETTS DEMOCRATS BREAK RANKS OVER NEW ABORTION LAW Pro-abortion members of Congress are also likely to urge the passage of the Women’s Health Protection Act. This bill is intended to codify the state of abortion extremism under Roe v. Wade, preventing any state or locality from restricting abortion before viability. If this became law, it would also erase necessary safeguards for women like mandatory ultrasounds to confirm pregnancy or rule out ectopic pregnancies, eliminate waiting periods and allow unrestricted mail-order abortion. Both the Hyde and Weldon amendments have survived pro-abortion majorities before, including the 117th Congress. What pro-life groups have more accurately called the "Women’s Health Endangerment Act" has been fended off since it was first introduced in 2013. Under the 117th Congress, this bill passed the House of Representatives but did not reach the 60-vote threshold needed to overcome cloture in the Senate. However, this new Congress is signaling less political restraint and may eliminate the filibuster to evade the necessary checks and balances of cloture. Pro-life groups must be unified in opposing this extreme tactic. It is essential to remember that Congress is only one cog in the political machine, and we can still fight for life within the Trump administration and among the many states. The pro-life movement has overcome many cycles of pro-abortion control since Roe and yet still was able to achieve the historic victory in Dobbs not too long after the 117th Congress. FIRST ON FOX: TOP REPUBLICANS TAKE ABORTION PILL FIGHT TO SUPREME COURT, CITING COERCION AND SAFETY RISKS Administrative agency action is still on the table. The Food and Drug Administration’s review of the abortion pill is still pending, and its latest update to the courts suggests final results will be available to the public by March 2027. Restoring in-person dispensing requirements as a minimum repair to mifepristone’s Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy is still on the table. It’s even more essential now that the agency’s review is airtight and able to withstand partisan scrutiny. The Trump administration still has the authority to finally rescind the Biden-era Office of Legal Counsel’s politicized Comstock opinion and fully enforce the law through the Department of Justice. Stopping the mail-order abortion scheme harming women across the country will be essential to combatting the losses of this week. Losses in Texas showed us that we cannot become complacent in protecting life where we believe it to be the most secure. articles.title: The 5 most consequential developments from a jaw-dropping election
articles.summary: Biggest unexpected consequence: The Supreme Court decision curtailing the Voting Rights Act, which helped fuel a "blacklash."
articles.body:
The nation's biggest political shift in a half-century sparked a flood of jaw-dropping headlines.

Democrats take control of the House and Senate, winning even in such deep red states as Kansas and South Carolina. Electoral breakthroughs for candidates who are Black, Hispanic, Native American and gay. A Democratic socialist elected mayor in the nation's second-largest city, Los Angeles, joining one elected last year in the largest, New York.

With the final votes now being counted from the Nov. 3 midterm elections, here are five of the most jaw-dropping developments of all − and ones with the biggest potential to have lasting repercussions ahead.

Texas Democrats, who had not won a statewide elected office since 1994, carried all of them.

Gina Hinojosa ousted Greg Abbott, the nation's longest-serving governor, and newcomer James Talarico defeated Ken Paxton, a fixture in Texas politics. Democratic candidates won races for lieutenant governor, attorney general, comptroller, land commissioner, agriculture commissioner and railroad commissioner, and they claimed seven statewide judicial elections, including four seats on the state's Supreme Court .

Candidates make history in race, gender and faith in 2026

The swing was stunning among Latino voters , who make up nearly a third of the state's eligible voters.

Hispanics who had swung to Donald Trump in 2024 snapped back to Democrats, especially in the Rio Grande Valley and other Texas border counties. That trend was nationwide: In exit polls sponsored by NBC News and other news organizations, Democrats carried Latinos by 30 percentage points, 64%-34%.

If Democrats can succeed in making the Lone Star State blue or even purple, that could have seismic repercussions for the calculations on how to carry the White House in 2028.

Among the four biggest states, Democrats have generally relied on California and New York while Republicans have counted on Florida and Texas.

It's been 50 years since Texas backed a Democrat for president. If it's no longer reliably red, the Electoral College could face its most fundamental realignment since then.

Most seismic shift by a voter group: Young people

In the 2024 presidential race, Trump scored major gains for a Republican among voters under 30 , who had been a Democratic-leaning group. He split them about evenly with Democrat Kamala Harris and carried a majority of young men.

But they didn't stick with the GOP the next time around. In the midterms, more than 7 of 10 younger voters cast their ballots for Democratic House candidates.

Notably, that included more than 6 in 10 younger voters who are White, a demographic that Trump had won by 10 points. And nearly 6 in 10 younger men, a reversal after Trump had carried 56% of them in 2024.

To be sure, young people were as usual less likely to vote than their elders. They made up just over 10% of the midterm electorate.

But their loyalty is clearly up for grabs − and they will be around to vote for decades more.

Biggest unintended consequence: Louisiana v. Callais

In April, the Supreme Court significantly limited the 1965 Voting Rights Act , allowing Louisiana to adopt a redistricting map that eliminated one of the state's two majority-Black congressional districts. By 6-3, a conservative majority set a new and higher standard for triggering the law's provisions, designed to protect minority voting rights.

In a dissent, Justice Elena Kagan warned that the decision left a key section of the Voting Rights Act "all but a dead letter," and the NAACP Legal Defense Fund called it "devastating."

But dismay over the decision ended up creating what has been dubbed a "blacklash," intensifying efforts by Black candidates and activists. In the midterms, Black governors were elected for the first time in Florida, Georgia, Nevada and Wisconsin.

That's more than the total number of Black governors elected ever − there have been three − and it included the first gubernatorial election ever of a Black woman, Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia.

Only two U.S. Senate races hadn't been called as of Nov. 8. One was in Alaska, which was expected to be close.

The other was in Mississippi. Which wasn't.

With 97% of the vote counted, Democrat Scott Colom led Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 49.1%-48.8%, a margin of 2,574 votes. That gives Colom a narrow lead but not a guaranteed victory.

It's been more than a decade since any Democrat won statewide office in Mississippi.

And it's been more than 150 years, since Reconstruction, that a Black candidate won statewide office there.

Shortest-lived voter coalition: Trump 2024

The coalition that sent Trump back to the White House two years ago has fractured .

In 2024, with an electorate dissatisfied with President Joe Biden 's leadership, especially on inflation, Trump made major gains among crucial voter groups. They included Black men and moderates as well as Hispanics and young people.

Voters are still dissatisfied on inflation and most are opposed to the war in Iran, which has driven up the price of fuel and more. Exit polls gave Trump a job-approval rating of 37% at the midterms, lower than Biden's job-approval rating of 41% on the eve of the 2024 election, which his vice president lost.

That's not the first time that declarations of a new governing coalition proved short-lived. Republicans predicted a realignment after George W. Bush's reelection in 2004, and Democrats did the same after Barack Obama's election in 2008.

But Bush was succeeded by Obama, then Obama by Trump as voters sought change.

"The American people clearly want change that's bold, change that's transformational and change that is dramatic," House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, the likely new House speaker, said on ABC's "This Week." "And that's everywhere."

"So I think even though the Democrats had a big night on Tuesday, that does not mean that the country is now all supportive of all the Democrat policies," Florida governor-elect Byron Donalds, a Republican, cautioned on NBC's "Meet the Press."

The question for Democrats now: Can they succeed in building a more durable coalition?

The Peach State's gubernatorial contest also went the Democrats way, electing former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Bottoms as the nation's first Black woman governor by about 9 percentage points. She will be first Democrat elected to lead Georgia since 1998. Democrats flipped at least seven seats in the Senate to gain a 54-seat majority in traditionally Republican states such as Texas, Kansas and South Carolina. (Carlos Barria, REUTERS)
Democrat Annie Andrews became the first woman Senator elected in South Carolina. (Win McNamee, Getty Images)
In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed beat his GOP opponent , becoming the nation's first Muslim U.S. senator. (Ryan Garza, USA TODAY Network)
Democrat David Crowley won Wisconsin’s governor race, becoming the first Black person to hold the office. (Jovanny Hernandez / Milwaukee Journal Sentinel)
Florida Democrat Pia Dandiya notched a historic first after becoming the first Indian American to be elected to Congress in the Sunshine state. (CRYSTAL VANDER WEIT/TCPALM)

Democrat Deb Haaland of New Mexico made history after being elected the first Native American woman to serve as a governor of any state. She previously made history as the first Native American woman in Congress and the first Native American woman in the Biden administration cabinet. (Jasper Colt, USA TODAY)
In Minnesota, Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, a citizen of the White Earth Band of Ojibwe, won the race to become the first Native American woman in the Senate. (TIM EVANS, AFP via Getty Images)
Democrat Dr. Amy Acton is the first woman elected governor of Ohio. (Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch)

articles.title: Musk spent big on Republicans in the midterms. He has little to show for it
articles.summary: Elon Musk poured millions of dollars into boosting Republicans in the midterm elections, but the tech mogul’s vast wealth was no match for the blue wave that...
articles.body:
Elon Musk poured millions of dollars into boosting Republicans in the midterm elections, but the tech mogul's vast wealth was no match for the blue wave that battered the GOP on Tuesday night.

Despite spending more than $442 million this cycle — a massive sum that eclipsed his support for President Trump in the 2024 election — Republicans lost ground across the country, even in territory considered relatively safe for the party.

The GOP's drubbing underscored the limits of the world's richest man in shaping the political map and raises questions about how his business empire will fare under Democratic leaders in his home base of Texas and on Capitol Hill.

"Other than the Republicans, Elon Musk is probably the biggest loser of last Tuesday," said Cayce Myers, a Virginia Tech public relations professor who has focused on political campaigns.

Musk pumped hundreds of millions of dollars into the 2024 presidential race and became a major figure in Trump's second term, even leading the cost-saving crackdown that led to sweeping cuts and layoffs in the federal government. But after pouring millions into a Wisconsin race that didn't pay off last year, Musk said he'd scale back political spending .

That pledge didn't hold for long, and Musk started midterm spending in late 2025 . By Election Day, he was the top donor by a mile.

"You have to have money to be competitive. No question," Myers added. "But money cannot guarantee outcome."

Brendan Steinhauser, a Texas-based Republican strategist and CEO of the Alliance for Secure AI, said "all of the money in the world cannot move voters when they have their minds made up." He also suggested the impact of Musk's spending in getting voters to turn out for Trump in 2024 was "overstated," noting that "money has diminishing returns in politics."

The billionaire's political losses Tuesday were starkest in his home state of Texas, where Musk spent at least $168 million boosting embattled Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton.

Paxton fell to Democrat James Talarico in the Texas Senate race — and Democrats flipped more than a half dozen other statewide roles, including the governor's office and the attorney general post, turning the state's top roles blue for the first time in decades.

The Texas Senate became the most expensive nonpresidential race on record, according to AdImpact data just before Election Day, with nearly $575 million spent on the Paxton-Talarico fight. In the general election stretch, pro-Paxton donors spent more than double the money that was spent by the pro-Talarico camp, with a major boost from Musk.

Musk also gave $5 million to Texas Gov. Greg Abbott's (R) reelection bid, according to campaign finance records, only for Abbott to lose to Democrat Gina Hinojosa — a state lawmaker who pledged to put a pause on data center expansion and won a court order last week seeking access to emails between Abbott's office and Musk.

Meanwhile, Paxton will be replaced as the state's top prosecutor by Democrat Nathan Johnson, who promised on the campaign trail to investigate grants to Musk's Starlink and SpaceX.

Democrats also broke into the GOP's trifecta control over the Texas state Legislature, flipping the House .

"He could have spent $0 and probably seen the same result," Steinhauser said. "This was a national wave election of historic proportions."

"Nobody was really prepared for it to be this big," he continued. "He could have spent $0. He could have spent $450 million in Texas and across the country, and it probably wouldn't have moved the needle very much."

The unexpected changing of the guard throughout Texas raises new questions about Musk's standing. Musk fled from California to Texas to escape left-wing politics and regulators .

"For Elon, the math ain't mathing," said Jon Taylor, a political science professor at the University of Texas at San Antonio. "All this to try to keep Texas red, but did he spend it essentially for nothing?"

"The thing that Musk, I think, needs to be worried about is that regulatory structure of the state of Texas is about to change, with an attorney general who's going to be aggressive against the Trump administration and against Elon Musk," Taylor said.

Musk himself seemed to read the results that way. "Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn't work this time," Musk wrote on the social platform X , which he owns.

"Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now," he said in another post, seemingly referencing SpaceX's recent push to develop orbital data centers.

Musk and his companies are also expected to be targets beyond Texas as Democrats take control on Capitol Hill.

Sen. Chris Coons (D-Del.) suggested on X last week that he'd investigate Musk's links to Russian President Vladimir Putin, after Putin touted the tech mogul as a "real genius."

Rep. James Walkinshaw (D-Va.) posted that Musk " must answer " for the cuts and firings undergone by the Department of Government Efficiency. Others have signaled they'll probe his companies' multibillion-dollar government contracts .

Stocks in Tesla and SpaceX fell by hundreds of billions of dollars in combined market value in the two days after the midterms amid investor concerns about new hurdles for the billionaire's companies under Democratic leadership, CNBC reported.

But Steinhauser was skeptical about how hard Democrats will go after Musk himself.

"I think the Democrats will be careful about overreach," he said. "There will be some questions about investigations and things like that ... but I don't think they're planning to just go after him personally in the way that maybe some might expect."

Texas-based Republican consultant Vinny Minchillo argued that "the business of Texas is business," regardless of the party in power.

"On one hand, listen, he spent a lot of money to support the Republicans, but on the other hand he's got a gigantic plant in Austin that employs a lot of people, puts a lot of money into the economy, and the SpaceX project does the same," Minchillo said of Musk.

"There was talk here that: Are the Democrats going to go after Elon Musk somehow? I'm hoping they're smarter than that."

Democrats might take aim at Musk and other billionaires' ability to spend so much on elections.

Talarico, for one, has accused Musk of trying to "buy his own personal U.S. senator" and called after the election for campaign finance reform.

"Somebody should not be able to spend that much money in politics, and I hope that we see reform that prevents that from happening," said Luke Warford, a founding partner at the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund.

At the same time, Warford forecast that Musk's business empire will remain a major player in the Lone Star State as the new crop of Democrats takes power.

"Elon is a person who brings a lot of innovation to the state," he said, "and so I think it's going to be really interesting to see how it plays out."
